History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
25-year-old female* with no significant past medical history presents with a 3-day history of persistent, severe, right-predominant headache with photophobia and transient visual phenomena, partially relieved by ibuprofen; migraine suspected. (*Age inferred as “adult”; exact age not provided.)

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Blinding” headache for 3 days, began suddenly on waking.  
• Course: Constant; intensity 8/10 dropping to ~5/10 with ibuprofen; never fully resolves.  
• Location/character: Diffuse but worst over right eye; described as stabbing when standing quickly or whipping head.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia; intermittent “shooting lights” in vision; mild nausea without vomiting; no tingling, numbness, weakness, fever, coryza, sinus pain, cough, epistaxis, weight change.  
• Sleep: Falls asleep without difficulty; headache does not wake her but present on waking.  
• Triggers/relievers: Worse with bright light and sudden positional changes; modest relief with ibuprofen; no complete relief.  
• Previous headaches: Occasional mild pressure between eyes; no prior migraines, aura, nausea, or vomiting.  
• Review of systems: Negative for focal neurological deficits, meningeal signs, constitutional symptoms, taste/smell changes, or recent travel.  

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• Childhood “pain” of unclear nature; resolved; no diagnosis (details limited).  

Medications:
• Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Ibuprofen OTC – dose/route/frequency not documented.  

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone.  
• Employment: Works from home; missed 1.5 workdays over last 3 days due to headache.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: ~3 alcoholic drinks once per week.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies.  

Family History:
• Mother suffers from migraines with vomiting.  
• No other familial illnesses disclosed.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed during tele-consult.)

Investigations:
• None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute severe headache, probable first episode migraine vs secondary cause  
  • Assessment: 3-day persistent unilateral-predominant headache with photophobia and visual aura-like description; no red-flag neuro deficits but duration >72 h warrants in-person evaluation.  
  • Plan:  
    – Arrange face-to-face appointment for full neurological exam, fundoscopy, and blood pressure check.  
    – Prescribe stronger NSAID (name/dose not specified in transcript) plus advise concurrent paracetamol; take with food.  
    – Educate on red-flag symptoms: worsening pain, new neuro deficits, change in character, or unbearable pain → attend A&E immediately.  

Issue 2 – Contraceptive pill and possible migraine with aura  
  • Assessment: Current combined oral contraceptive may be contraindicated if migraine with aura confirmed.  
  • Plan: Re-assess contraceptive suitability at in-person visit; consider alternative method if migraine with aura diagnosed.  

Issue 3 – Work impact and symptomatic relief  
  • Assessment: Headache interfering with daily function and work productivity.  
  • Plan: Provide medical certificate if needed; discuss lifestyle modifications (hydration, regular meals, screen breaks, reduced bright-light exposure).

General plan items:  
  • Monitor symptoms; cancel appointment if headache fully resolves.  
  • Provide contact details for support line for interim advice.

• No internal transcript conflicts noted.
